architectureExercise.title: 20-minute embedded platform and product exercise
architectureExercise.prompt: Design and defend a common embedded software platform for three product families using MCU control, Embedded Linux, Android/AAOS, connectivity and OTA.
structure: Clarify customer outcomes, product variants and non-functional constraints.
Partition hardware, firmware, RTOS, Linux, Android, cloud and product responsibilities.
Define common services, extension points, APIs and compatibility commitments.
Explain timing, performance, security, update, rollback and field observability.
Create roadmap increments, team ownership, supplier contracts and release evidence.
Make one difficult product or schedule trade-off and state who accepts the residual risk.
challenges: One product requires a 1 ms control loop while another prioritizes rich HMI.
A supplier BSP becomes unsupported before end of product life.
An Android customization blocks the next AOSP migration.
A shared OTA campaign fails on one hardware variant.
A commercial launch date conflicts with an unresolved severe defect.
Two regions demand incompatible common-feature priorities.

days.title: Embedded Systems Foundations
days.focus: Execution models, constraints, MCU/MPU/SoC selection, hardware/software partitioning and lifecycle.
days.deliverable: Create a boundary and constraint map for a connected embedded controller.

days.title: Processor, Memory and Hardware Interfaces
days.focus: CPU modes, memory hierarchy, MMU/MPU, interrupts, DMA, watchdogs and peripheral buses.
days.deliverable: Produce a memory, interrupt and data-movement design for a sensor gateway.

days.title: Firmware, Boot and BSP Architecture
days.focus: Reset flow, startup code, linker control, bootloaders, BSPs, drivers, updates and recovery.
days.deliverable: Draw a verified-boot and rollback flow from reset vector to application.

days.title: RTOS, Concurrency and Timing
days.focus: Scheduling, synchronization, priority inversion, ISR design, timing analysis and multicore effects.
days.deliverable: Build a task, interrupt and resource model with response-time budgets.

days.title: Embedded Linux Platform Engineering
days.focus: Boot chain, kernel/user space, device model, Device Tree, drivers, build systems, tracing and hardening.
days.deliverable: Diagnose a Linux device bring-up and performance problem end to end.

days.title: Android Platform and Android Automotive
days.focus: Android boot, Binder, HAL/AIDL, system services, permissions, SELinux, AAOS and Vehicle HAL.
days.deliverable: Trace a vehicle signal from HAL to an AAOS application and back.

days.title: Connectivity, Infotainment and OTA
days.focus: Networking, multimedia, telematics, cloud integration, secure OTA, rollback and field operations.
days.deliverable: Design an OTA-capable connected infotainment feature with recovery and observability.

days.title: Reusable Platforms and Product Variability
days.focus: Product-line architecture, commonality, variants, APIs, compatibility, suppliers and platform governance.
days.deliverable: Define a common feature platform for three vehicle or machine families.

days.title: Performance, Security, Quality and Release
days.focus: CPU/memory/latency analysis, secure boot, keys, testing, reliability, release readiness and field monitoring.
days.deliverable: Create a release evidence and risk decision package for a shared embedded platform.

days.title: Engineering and Product Leadership
days.focus: Technical strategy, roadmaps, backlog, matrix leadership, architecture governance and product accountability.
days.deliverable: Present a platform strategy and resolve a quality-versus-schedule conflict.

quiz.q: Which property most strongly separates a hard real-time requirement from a high-performance requirement?
quiz.why: Hard real-time classification depends on the consequence of missing a deadline, not average speed.

quiz.q: What does an MMU primarily add compared with an MPU?
quiz.why: An MMU translates addresses and supports virtual-memory isolation; other controls require separate mechanisms.

quiz.q: Which design most reduces risk during interrupted OTA activation?
options: A/B or transactional activation with trusted metadata
quiz.why: Transactional or A/B activation preserves a known-good state and explicit recovery path.

quiz.q: What is a common cause of Binder service deadlock?
quiz.why: Synchronous call chains combined with lock ownership or callbacks can create cycles and thread starvation.

quiz.q: Which is the best platform metric?
options: Product lead-time and quality improvement from adoption
quiz.why: A platform exists to improve product outcomes; asset counts alone encourage unhelpful abstraction.

quiz.q: Why can low average CPU coexist with deadline misses?
options: Blocking, interrupts and shared-resource contention create tail latency
quiz.why: Real-time behavior is driven by worst-case interference and blocking, not only average utilization.

quiz.q: What is the final purpose of secure boot?
quiz.why: Secure boot authenticates the execution chain; it does not guarantee vulnerability-free software.

quiz.q: What should a common-feature product owner optimize?
options: Customer value and technical integrity across the product family
quiz.why: The role balances shared value, product variation, architecture and lifecycle commitments.

quiz.q: What should happen first during a cross-team field incident?
options: Create a shared incident lead, impact statement and evidence timeline
quiz.why: A common command structure and evidence model enable containment and coordinated diagnosis.

quiz.q: When is an architecture exception healthy?
options: When time-bounded, owned, risk-assessed and paired with a migration decision
Whenever a product date is near
quiz.why: Bounded exceptions preserve delivery flexibility without silently becoming permanent architecture.
